errors.text: The targeted property is misidentified as saturation magnetization; the target concerns improving coercivity beyond the approximately 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys.
The material is treated as a generic single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-derived alloy rather than the dual-phase fcc/C14 FeCoNiTi alloy central to the target.

The proposed orbital-moment challenge—quantification and reversal of crystal-field quenching—does not match the target challenge of establishing how a small orbital moment contributes to coercivity through C14-assisted spin canting and domain-wall pinning.
The hypothesis omits the key comparison with the compositionally matched C14-dominant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 alloy and the observed coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.

The cited evidence primarily concerns CrMnFeCoNi/Cantor-type alloys and longitudinal spin fluctuations, and does not substantiate the claims about orbital-moment enhancement or saturation magnetization in FeCoNiTi.
